Minimum Variance Analysis on the Magnetic Field¶

Here, I try to reproduce the paper, Romaneli et al., 2016, JGR, "Proton cyclotron waves occurrence rate upstream fromMars observed by MAVEN: Associated variability of the Martian upper atmosphere".

Reference: https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/2016JA023270 https://www.researchgate.net/publication/234549390_Minimum_Variance_Analysis_Cluster_Themes

Apply the MVA method to the magnetic field data¶

The purpose of this method is to find a vector that makes the following variance minimum (or maximum), given 3D magnetic field data, $$\sigma^2=\frac{1}{N}\sum_k^N({\bf B}_k\cdot{\bf x}-<{\bf B}_k\cdot{\bf x}>)^2,$$ where $k$ is the data point and $<\cdot>$ is a mean.

To find the vector ${\bf x}$ that minises the variance, the easiest way is probably to solve the following equation, $${\bf Mx}=\lambda{\bf x},$$ where ${\bf M}=<B_iB_j>-<B_i><B_j>$, $\lambda$ is the eigenvalue, and ${\bf x}$ is the eigenvector.

In [105]:
bxyz=data['MVN_MAG_L2-SUNSTATE-1SEC']['OB_B'][:,:].sel(time=slice(start, end)).values

Mb=np.zeros((3,3))

for i in range(3):
    for j in range(3):
        Mb[i,j]=np.mean(bxyz[:,i]*bxyz[:,j])-np.mean(bxyz[:,i])*np.mean(bxyz[:,j])

v,w=np.linalg.eig(Mb)

sorted_indices = np.argsort(v)

v_sort=v[sorted_indices]
w_sort=w[:,sorted_indices]

print(w_sort)

### define new IMFs based on the MVA ###
bnew1=np.dot(bxyz[:,:],w_sort[:,2])
bnew2=np.dot(bxyz[:,:],w_sort[:,1])
bnew3=np.dot(bxyz[:,:],w_sort[:,0])


### display values ###
from IPython.display import Math
display(Math(r'\lambda_1=%.4f,\: \lambda_2=%.4f,\: \lambda_3=%.4f' %(v_sort[2],v_sort[1],v_sort[0])))
display(Math(r'\lambda_1/\lambda_2=%.4f,\: \lambda_2/\lambda_3=%.4f' %(v_sort[2]/v_sort[1],v_sort[1]/v_sort[0])))
display(Math(r'{\bf B}_0=[%.4f, %.4f, %.4f]' %(np.mean(bnew1),np.mean(bnew2),np.mean(bnew3))))

### plot figures ###
plt.figure(figsize=(12,4))

plt.subplot(121)
plt.plot(bnew2[0],bnew1[0],'o')
plt.plot(bnew2[2],bnew1[2],'ro')
plt.plot(bnew2,bnew1,'.-')
plt.xlabel(r'$B_2$ [nT]')
plt.ylabel(r'$B_1$ [nT]')
#plt.xlim(-0.25,1.75)

plt.subplot(122)
plt.plot(bnew3,bnew2)
plt.xlim(-5.7,-3.7)

plt.ylabel(r'$B_2$ [nT]')
#plt.ylim(-0.25,1.75)

plt.show()
